primitives.verbatim_quote: An injury of any severity to the developing brain can disrupt a child's developmental trajectory and may result in restrictions in school and participation in activities (e.g., sports).

primitives.name: Post-TBI Cognitive Residual Effects

primitives.name: Fragmented Service Delivery System

primitives.name: Diagnostic Evidence Gap
primitives.verbatim_quote: To date, most evidence available for the management of pediatric mTBI is level B (inconsistent or limited-quality patient-oriented evidence [examples: small cohort studies, case studies, and control trials with limitations]) or C (consensus, usual practice, opinion, or weaker-level evidence).93 38

primitives.assumptions: Evidence levels B and C indicate insufficient statistical power or methodological rigor for reliable clinical inference.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When E = B or C, diagnostic confidence intervals expand beyond acceptable thresholds for pediatric mTBI.

primitives.name: Sleep Hygiene Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: REPORT TO CONGRESS Recognizing the lack of evidence-based pediatric mTBI guidelines, the CDC's National Center for Injury Prevention and Control's (NCIPC) Board of Scientific Counselors (BSC) created the Pediatric Mild Traumatic Brain Injury Guideline Workgroup to inform the development of a guideline.
